headline: Extended moratorium ordinance on mobile home park lot rent increases, effective September 29, 2026.
summary: The Council held a public hearing where many mobile home park residents spoke in favor of extending the rent moratorium, citing rising lot rents and fixed incomes. Several park owners and other residents spoke against the ordinance, questioning the process and the need for the ordinance. The Council voted 4-0 to give final passage to the moratorium ordinance extension.
decisions: Approved final passage of the Moratorium Ordinance regarding Rent Increases for Lots in Mobile Home Parks, effective September 29, 2026, by a 4-0 roll call vote.

decision_evidence.quote: That the proposed Moratorium Ordinance regarding Rent Increases for Lots in Mobile Home Parks, to be effective September 29, 2026, receive final passage by a roll call vote. Passed - Vote 4-0

CITY OF LEWISTON 
 
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 26, 2026 
 
SPECIAL MEETING HELD IN THE COUNCIL ROOM AT 6:00 P.M. 
 
THE HONORABLE CARL L. SHELINE, MAYOR, PRESIDING. 
          
PRESENT: Mayor Sheline, Councilors Nagine, Harriman, and Chittim, City Administrator 
Bryan Kaenrath and Deputy City Administrator Brian O’Malley. Absent/Excused: Councilors 
Longchamps, Roy, Noble, and Martel. Note – Per the City Charter, the Mayor is permitted to 
cast a vote in the absence of a City Councilor.  
 
Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag. 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FINAL PASSAGE FOR AN EXTENSION OF THE 
MORATORIUM ORDINANCE REGARDING RENT INCREASES FOR LOTS IN 
MOBILE HOME PARKS 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. 
 
Bret Martel, Ward 7 – This is not just an issue of a lot rent moratorium but a failure of Lewiston 
government to provide transparency, leadership, and accountability. Asked last evening after the 
special meeting if the City Attorney and Housing Committee chair would be present to address 
questions and no response was provided. When shootings were occurring in city, asked for an 
agenda item to address and was denied because it was submitted a day late. Why is this issue 
now an urgent matter with a special meeting? A five-year member of the Housing Committee 
resigned citing concerns with lack of transparency and accountability. 
 
Andrew Jones, Ward 2 – Concerns with process that has taken place. This is the third attempt at 
this issue but we are not addressing pressing issues such as gun violence. If City Attorney 
recommended this meeting, he could be here to explain why. The Council is the client and has 
the authority to release the information. Several Councilors are not here; one choosing not to 
participate and is sitting in audience in protest. 
 
Eric Fleishman, Lewiston – Thank you for the special meeting. Good to see people taking this 
matter seriously.  This is an urgent matter to address now because of the potential time gap 
between the expiration of the current moratorium and adoption of the ordinance regulating lot 
rents. During that time, rents could increase substantially knowing they will be controlled later. 
Several parks raised their lot rents when the state discussed the idea of controlling lot rents. 
Parks raised the rents in anticipation of that passing, even though it did not pass, the lot rent 
amounts did not decrease, some went up $150 a month. Some residents are facing the choice of 
rents vs food or rents vs health insurance. It is essential for the city to regulate increases in order 
to control homelessness.  
 
Valerie Jackson, Ward 6 – Fox Run Mobile Home Park resident.  When Beauvita bought park, 
implemented a 10% lot rent increase. Her monthly rent went from $500 to $550 a month. New 
residents are $600 a month.  She pays for snow removal and lawn maintenance w hich is about 
$200 a month. She also pays for water and sewer to the park owners. Her mortgage costs are on

top of these expenses. The potential time gap between the moratorium and new ordinance creates 
too much exposure for time to have rents increase. Lots of retirees live in mobile home parks, 
cannot increase income, a vulnerable population that could become homeless if rents increase too 
much. Please extend moratorium. 
 
Kathy Wing, Fox Run mobile home park resident – With new state law, expecting an annual lot 
increase of $100 a year. She and husband work part time after retiring so they can afford 
expenses. Understanding is that the lot rent ordinance will be presented in September. Please 
pass to help prevent corporate landlords from hurting tenants. 
 
Louise Martel, Ward 6 – Fox Run Mobile Park, 30-year resident. Last night, the regional 
manager of the company that owns the park said the basic lot rents are $420 but this is untrue. 
She as a thirty-year tenant pays $550 a month, and new residents pay $600 a month. Lot renters 
have no control or say in operations. Please support moratorium. 
 
Danielle Fournier, Ward 6 – Resident of Fox Run Mobile Park, residents live on fixed income. 
Listened last night to business owners cannot afford to operate the parks if the lot rents are 
controlled by ordinance, the owners tried to equate their issues of balancing their business 
expenses with the same issues that tenants face balancing their costs. In the first half of 2021, the 
lot rent was $365 a month; in the last half of the year, it was increased to $385. As of July 2022, 
it increased to $405. In July 2023, it went up to $450 and in July 2024, it went to $500. Beauvita 
purchased the park then and increased the rents to $550. New residents have to pay $600 but no 
new services have been added, so this is just corporate greed.  If moratorium was not in effect, 
the rent in July 2026 would probably have increased to $600. This all reflects a 78% increase in 
5 years, with an average of 15.6% a year and that is unsustainable. Please extend moratorium. 
 
John Gerry, Ward 6 – Resident of Fox Run, at last night’s meeting, struck by the many 
comments that there was no proof offered that the park owners have been acting in a predatory 
manner. It was noted last night that the rents in the parks owned by Beauvita have only gone up 
$37 since 2004. This is not true, within weeks of purchasing the park, they raised the rents $50 a 
month. Park representatives last night stated they need to raise rents to cover expenses in their 
other parks, it is not fair for the tenants of one park to have to pay a higher lot rent for 
improvements at another park.  Please extend the moratorium.  
 
Laurie Horton, Ward 2 – Last night’s vote showed you chose not to trust park owners. The 
special meetings do not demonstrate transparency; there are two meetings in September before 
the moratorium expires and it could have been handled then.  Why wasn’t it noticed before that 
the lot rent ordinance would not be ready in time and allow for the moratorium extension vote to 
occur at a regular meeting. The state laws allow one increase a year. Owners of the parks are not 
in business for subsidized housing; these businesses are for profit. The lot rent stabilization 
ordinance will make people homeless. 
 
John Horton, Ward 2 – It is clear that no data will change the minds of Councilors, the data 
shows this ordinance is not needed but the Council is choosing to not listen to the data. This 
meeting was called with very short notice, heard about it from one of his tenants. Statements that 
rents could triple without the lot rent ordinance are ridiculous. He has been very open, showed 
his company expenses to the Housing Committee so they can see the costs of operations, has 
been open to make sure that everything is open and fair. Has attended every Housing Committee
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 26, 2026 
                             
3 
 
meeting. The language in the moratorium ordinance is incorrect – eight out of the fourteen 
Whereas Claus statements have been proven to be false or not realistic at all.  This issue is not 
building trust in the community. 
 
Chris Saroie, Ward 1 – There is a perception that landlords are rich and greedy and unethical in 
their practices, and that is very offensive and untrue for some of us. The lot rents at Sunset 
Gardens Mobile Home Parks are $386 a month, including water and sewer. We have been fair 
and responsible park owners. With comments from the Council, such as “rents could triple if the 
moratorium lapses,” shows the Council does not trust park owners. What business owner would 
want to conduct business in Lewiston with that type of attitude and lack of trust from the 
Council?   
 
The Mayor then closed the hearing. 
 
Councilor Harriman announced that Councilor Noble had a prior commitment tonight and could 
not attend.  
 
 
VOTE (1) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Harriman: 
 
That the proposed Moratorium Ordinance regarding Rent Increases for Lots in Mobile Home 
Parks, to be effective September 29, 2026, receive final passage by a roll call vote. 
 
Passed - Vote 4-0 
 
 
VOTE (2) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To adjourn at 6:36 P.M.  Passed - Vote 4-0 
 
A true record, Attest: 
 
 
 
Brian T. O’Malley  
Deputy City Administrator 
Lewiston, Maine
